title: Uniform seminorm estimate for a single symbol with a dilated frequency cutoff
statement:
Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and the symbol estimates of [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators]. Fix integers $m\geq1$, $p,q\geq0$. For an integer $s$, a smooth map $a:\mathbf R^m\times\mathbf R^m\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(\mathbf C^p,\mathbf C^q)$ is in the uniform symbol class $S^s$ if every quantity
$$P_{s,n}(a)=\max_{|\alpha|,|\beta|\leq n}\sup_{x,\xi}(1+|\xi|)^{-s+|\beta|}\|\partial_x^\alpha\partial_\xi^\beta a(x,\xi)\|$$
is finite, for $n\in\mathbf N$. Let $\theta:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf R$ be smooth, equal to $0$ on $|\xi|\leq1$ and to $1$ on $|\xi|\geq2$. Put $\theta_R(\xi)=\theta(\xi/R)$ for $R\geq1$. For every $n\in\mathbf N$ there is a finite $C_n\geq1$, depending only on $m,n,\theta$, such that for every $s,t\in\mathbf Z$ with $t\geq s$, every $a\in S^s$ and every $R\geq1$, the product $(x,\xi)\mapsto\theta_R(\xi)a(x,\xi)$ belongs to $S^t$ and satisfies
$$P_{t,n}(\theta_R a)\leq C_n P_{s,n}(a)(1+R)^{s-t}.$$

source.place: WANTED locally: Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §3.7, printed pp.7–8, cutoff proof of asymptotic expansions, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf. The supplemental notes are distinct from the locally missing hodge-ams.pdf; this is the source actually read.

proof.text: Fix $n$. There are only finitely many pairs of multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$ with $|\alpha|,|\beta|\le n$, so it suffices to bound each weighted derivative. Write $d=t-s\ge0$.

source.place: §3.7 p.7, reduction to finitely many derivatives in a fixed seminorm.

proof.text: For each $|\gamma|\le n$, apply [lem-sfb-symbol-cutoff-scaled-derivatives]. Thus $\partial^\gamma\theta_R$ has size at most $A_n(1+R)^{-|\gamma|}$; when $|\gamma|>0$ it is supported in the annulus $R\le|\xi|\le2R$, while $\theta_R$ itself vanishes for $|\xi|\le R$. The same cited statement gives smoothness of $\theta_R$, needed in step 3.

source.place: §3.7 p.7, scaled cutoff derivative estimate and support.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-symbol-product-derivative-bound] with $u=v=m$ and $h=\theta_R$. It gives smoothness of the product and the explicit mixed Leibniz formula
$$\partial_x^\alpha\partial_\xi^\beta(\theta_Ra)=\sum_{\gamma\leq\beta}\binom\beta\gamma(\partial^\gamma\theta_R)(\partial_x^\alpha\partial_\xi^{\beta-\gamma}a),$$
together with the norm bound by the corresponding sum of products. In particular only derivatives of $a$ with $|\alpha|,|\beta-\gamma|\leq n$ occur.

source.place: §3.7 p.7, Leibniz formula after the scaled cutoff estimate.

proof.text:
Put $M=P_{s,n}(a)$, $d=t-s\geq0$ and $k=|\gamma|$. By the definition of $M$, the norm of $\partial_x^\alpha\partial_\xi^{\beta-\gamma}a$ is at most $M(1+|\xi|)^{s-|\beta|+k}$. The weighted norm of a Leibniz summand is therefore at most
$$A_nM(1+R)^{-k}(1+|\xi|)^{k-d}.$$
For $k=0$ its support has $|\xi|\geq R$, giving $(1+|\xi|)^{-d}\leq(1+R)^{-d}$. For $k>0$ its support has $R\leq|\xi|\leq2R$, giving $(1+|\xi|)^k\leq2^k(1+R)^k$ and $(1+|\xi|)^{-d}\leq(1+R)^{-d}$. Thus every weighted summand is bounded by $2^nA_nM(1+R)^{-d}$, including points where it vanishes. Summing the coefficients gives $\sum_{\gamma\leq\beta}\binom\beta\gamma=2^{|\beta|}\leq2^n$, by the coordinatewise binomial formula. Take $C_n=4^nA_n\geq1$. This is independent of $s,t,a,R,p,q$.

source.place: §3.7 p.7, substitution of cutoff and symbol estimates into the Leibniz formula.

proof.text: Step 3 gives smoothness. Step 4 bounds every weighted mixed derivative with $|\alpha|,|\beta|\leq n$ by the same number, uniformly in $x,\xi$. Taking their suprema and finite maximum proves $P_{t,n}(\theta_Ra)\leq C_nP_{s,n}(a)(1+R)^{s-t}$. Since this holds for each $n$ and $a\in S^s$, all the defining seminorms of $\theta_Ra$ in $S^t$ are finite. Hence $\theta_Ra\in S^t$.

source.place: §3.7 p.7, conclusion that the cutoff product has the required symbol-order estimates.

from.place: Supporting cutoff argument in the proof of det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images (3), Demailly §3.7 p.7: scaled cutoff derivative estimate and Leibniz weighted seminorm calculation.

split_report.summary: The five-step proof cites a scalar-cutoff derivative/support lemma and a general mixed coordinate Leibniz lemma, both statement-only. The remaining proof is the explicit symbol-weight calculation with C_n=4^n A_n. Full iterated-derivative norm bounds in Mathlib were rejected as an exact match because they do not give the separate mixed frequency orders used here. Checked n=0, R=1, t=s, arbitrary negative orders, zero matrix spaces, and boundary radii.
split_report.blueprint: The steps realize the supporting cutoff argument in the proof of det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images (3), specifically Demailly §3.7 p.7: scaled cutoff derivative estimate, Leibniz estimate, and weighted seminorm conclusion.

This is a first split (no 2026-10-21 re-split note): the item had no proof on the base (Q36 snapshot) and its statement is byte-identical. Demailly §3.7 pp.7-8 is not available locally (marked WANTED, proof_origin agent), so I checked every estimate myself. Steps: (1) finitely many (α,β), elementary. (2) lem-sfb-symbol-cutoff-scaled-derivatives gives exactly what is used: θ_R smooth, |∂^γθ_R|≤A_n(1+R)^{-|γ|}, θ_R=0 for |ξ|≤R, and ∂^γθ_R supported in R≤|ξ|≤2R for k>0. (3) lem-sfb-symbol-product-derivative-bound with u=v=m, h=θ_R: its hypotheses hold, and it gives the mixed Leibniz formula and norm bound with |β-γ|≤n. (4) Weighted term A_nM(1+R)^{-k}(1+|ξ|)^{k-d}. For k=0, |ξ|>R gives (1+R)^{-d}. For k>0, 1+|ξ|≤2(1+R) on the annulus, and the two factors are handled separately, so the sign of k-d does not matter. The binomial sum is 2^{|β|}≤2^n, so C_n=4^nA_n depends only on m,n,θ. Elementary. (5) Supremum and maximum, smoothness from step 3. Cutoff node is true: ∂^γθ_R=R^{-k}(∂^γθ)(ξ/R), R^{-k}≤2^k(1+R)^{-k}, derivatives vanish off the closed annulus by continuity, and θ is bounded. Product node is the standard multivariate Leibniz rule. Both nodes are generic, strictly smaller than the item, statement-only and self-contained (B1-B4). Tested on m=1, R=1, t=s, large d, negative orders, p=0 or q=0, β=0 and the boundary radii.
